newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lawyers demand release of Burundi's Bagaza.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers demand release of Burundi's Bagaza.

text.p: Lawyers for Burundi's ex-president Jean-Baptiste Bagaza demanded on Friday his release from house arrest, saying he was being held arbitrarily and denied the right to legal defence.

Lawyers Fethi Sahli and Laurent Ibara, in a statement issued in Paris, asked the Burindi government to "immediately and unconditionally end (Bagaza's) illegal, authoritarian, purely arbitrary arrest which is contrary to human rights".
They said his continued detention could have serious consequences amid Burundi's ethnic tension.
Bagaza, an ethnic Tutsi who was ousted from power in 1987, was placed under house arrest three weeks ago. Police said they raided his house and found guns, grenades and subversive papers.
Bagaza has been fiercely critical of President Pierre Buyoya, who took power in a military coup last July and had also ousted Bagaza from power in 1987.
